object_context: Child of H4d1. Fix a smooth projective family f:X->S, a rational Hodge-locus branch T through s0, and a chosen algebraic central witness z0 for a flat rational Hodge class alpha. Determine whether the geometric obstructions generated specifically by lifting z0 along T lie in an independently defined, computable envelope B_{T,m} on which the relevant Hodge/semiregularity detector is injective at every required Artin order. This is a propagation problem from an already algebraic witness; it does not address root initial algebraicity.
structural_coordinates: exact root coefficients are rational; integral Hodge counterexamples are outside the root contract
ambient fibers are smooth projective complex varieties; the active branch lies inside the Hodge locus of a fixed flat rational class
the chosen central witness may be a signed rational cycle; any local witness category must preserve coefficient bookkeeping
Hodge persistence constrains base directions but does not by itself imply geometric witness liftability
full semiregularity asks for detector faithfulness on the full obstruction space; H4d1a asks only for faithfulness on an independently described branch-generated envelope
the envelope must be defined from geometry, deformation maps, branch tangent data, or a derived obstruction complex before observing desired obstruction vanishing
first-order tangent or obstruction control is insufficient unless the construction persists compatibly through higher Artin orders
a zero branch envelope is a legitimate strict-weaker boundary control but may be vacuous for discovering a coupled lifting mechanism
formal lifting, algebraization, monodromy/global continuation, and root initial existence remain separate downstream obligations
higher codimension may require cotangent-complex/perfect-complex obstruction objects rather than a single normal-sheaf H^1
equivalent_formulations: restrict the geometric obstruction map to deformation directions induced by the Hodge-locus branch and identify its image inside the full obstruction group
construct a branch-reachable obstruction subobject B_{T,m} and test injectivity of the semiregularity/Hodge detector only on that subobject
compare the tangent/obstruction theory of a chosen cycle-witness space over T with the cohomological equations defining T, keeping the kernel of the detector explicit
seek a reduced obstruction theory adapted to the chosen Hodge branch whose obstruction sheaf is strictly smaller than the unrestricted witness obstruction sheaf
solved_analogues: codimension-one divisor/Picard deformation, where a relative line bundle or divisor can provide an explicit geometric lift
semiregular lci/subvariety settings where the semiregularity map annihilates obstructions and, under additional injectivity hypotheses, Hodge persistence controls geometric deformation
near_solved_analogues: Kloosterman's variational Hodge result for complete-intersection cycles on hypersurfaces, where flag-Hilbert and Hodge-locus tangent calculations identify a geometric locus in a special family
derived reduced obstruction theory attached to Buchweitz-Flenner semiregularity as developed by Pridham
Liu-Shen's analytic description of Hodge loci and Beltrami-differential criterion for variational Hodge questions, useful for specifying base directions but not by itself a cycle-witness theorem

method_transfers.source_context: Buchweitz-Flenner semiregularity and Pridham's derived reduced obstruction theory
method_transfers.method: factor geometric obstruction information through a semiregularity/reduced-obstruction map, then isolate the part of the obstruction theory actually visible to the target deformation problem
shared_structure: chosen algebraic witness with a deformation functor
geometric obstructions mapped to Hodge/cohomological data
possibility of replacing a full obstruction space by a reduced one
required_assumptions: a source-bound semiregularity or derived obstruction map exists for the witness category
the branch-induced obstruction subobject is functorially defined before vanishing is known
injectivity/faithfulness is proved on that subobject rather than assumed
disanalogies: global annihilation of obstructions by a semiregularity map does not automatically provide injectivity on the geometric obstruction space
a reduced obstruction theory can remove directions without proving that all branch-generated lifts algebraize globally
method_transfers.repair_question: Can the branch T canonically define a proper reduced obstruction subobject whose inclusion and detector restriction are computable and stable across Artin order?

method_transfers.source_context: Nishinou relative deformation of semiregular pairs/divisors
method_transfers.method: express the next relative obstruction from the ambient Kodaira-Spencer direction and use Hodge persistence plus detector faithfulness to force its vanishing
shared_structure: ambient family direction produces a geometric obstruction class
Hodge persistence supplies a cohomological vanishing condition
chosen witness is already algebraic on the central fiber
required_assumptions: the relevant relative obstruction class is explicitly identified
the semiregularity detector is sufficiently faithful on the generated obstruction directions
iteration hypotheses persist to the required order
disanalogies: Nishinou's stated theorem is in a special semiregular setting and does not establish a weaker branch-restricted criterion for arbitrary higher-codimension cycles
the root rational Hodge problem permits signed rational combinations and arbitrary codimension
method_transfers.repair_question: Which subspace is actually reached by branch Kodaira-Spencer directions before semiregularity is invoked, and can detector faithfulness be proved only there?

method_transfers.source_context: Kloosterman variational Hodge conjecture for complete-intersection cycles on hypersurfaces
method_transfers.method: compare a geometric flag-Hilbert locus with the Hodge locus using exact tangent-space calculations and dimension/smoothness control

Hodge locus and geometric witness locus map to the same base
tangent directions can be computed independently on both sides
required_assumptions: the cycle has the special complete-intersection geometry of the source theorem
the flag-Hilbert parameter space and Artinian-Gorenstein tangent calculation apply
dimension/smoothness equalities needed to upgrade tangent comparison are verified
disanalogies: special hypersurface complete intersections are far from arbitrary rational cycles
tangent equality alone is not an all-order obstruction-envelope theorem
method_transfers.repair_question: Can the source tangent calculation be reinterpreted as an independently defined branch-reachable obstruction envelope, and which part survives outside complete-intersection geometry?

method_transfers.source_context: Liu-Shen analytic Hodge-map description on Kuranishi families

explicit characterization of directions preserving type (p,p)

formal lifting does not imply algebraization, monodromy control, or global domination

cross_domain_analogies.source_situation: A system may have a large ambient state/error space, while a restricted family of inputs reaches only a smaller subspace. Stability or observability need only be checked on the reachable subspace for that input family, provided reachability is defined independently of the desired stability conclusion.
common_abstraction: full ambient obstruction space versus branch-reachable obstruction space
restricted input/base directions generate only part of the ambient response
faithfulness can be weaker when required only on the independently computed reachable part
source_to_target_mapping: allowed control inputs -> tangent/Artin directions of Hodge branch T
reachable error states -> geometric witness obstructions generated along T
unobservable modes outside reachability -> detector kernel directions never generated by T
shared_constraints: the restricted subspace must be computed before testing success
modes outside the reachable subspace cannot certify or refute branch-specific lifting
all-order dynamics may enlarge the reachable set relative to first order
disanalogies: deformation functors are nonlinear/algebro-geometric rather than linear control systems
obstruction spaces and maps can change with Artin order
algebraization and monodromy have no generic control-theory analogue
cross_domain_analogies.proposed_principle: Replace full semiregularity by detector faithfulness on an independently constructed branch-reachable obstruction envelope, then test whether the envelope remains proper and stable beyond first order.
cross_domain_analogies.validation_obligation: After the strict gate, produce one source-bound non-semiregular positive control where the branch envelope is provably smaller than the full obstruction space, then seek a coupled example with a nonzero proper envelope and test the next Artin order.
cross_domain_analogies.provenance_note: Structural proposal analogy only; it supplies no Hodge-theorem authority.

analogy_scan_notes: Scanned reduced obstruction theory, relative semiregularity, special variational-Hodge families, explicit Hodge-locus equations, and restricted-input/reachable-subspace analogies. Retained only the reachable-subspace analogy because it produces an exact anti-tautology obligation and an adversarial strict-weaker calibration.
